sources.entry: Vigil - Native terminal that runs manager-led trees of coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode), with worker results rolling up as summaries while every node keeps its own TUI.

summary.one_liner: Vigil is a native macOS terminal app that runs manager-led trees of coding agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode), where workers report summaries up to their manager while each node keeps its own native TUI.
use_cases: Split a large coding task across a manager agent and parallel worker agents
Mix Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode in one orchestrated tree
Audit what each coding agent did by replaying its transcript
Resume a finished multi-agent session from its saved tree
Keep a manager agent's context small by rolling up worker summaries
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (URL is blank in the README)
notable: Manager-worker tree where detail flows down and summaries roll up to keep context lean
Every node is the agent CLI's own native TUI, so you can take over any node directly
Complete session history with read-only replay and Enter-to-resume through each CLI's native mechanism
Settings live in JSON files under ~/.config/vigil/ with no settings panel
All global shortcuts are Command-modified so keys pass through to the agent TUI
caveats: Pre-1.0 and under active development; config surface and defaults may change
Requires at least one agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode) on PATH
Agents are spawned directly without a login shell, so shell aliases and .zshrc exports do not apply
